_comment: Corrections to the box membership recorded in cards.json, keyed by box key. Each entry is authoritative for that box: on load the box is stripped from every card's containedIn, then re-added from the list here. Card ids map to quantityPerBox. Use this when the community data groups a set wrongly, rather than editing cards.json, which is regenerated from the builder bundle.

LAB_PD_REAPER_TYPE_1._note: The community data put four Reaper variants in this one box at 1 each. The product listing sells each Reaper alone, 2 copies per box, matching how Type E was already recorded.

LAB_PD_REAPER_TYPE_2._note: Was empty in the community data; MD-4B was filed under the Type 1 box.

COMBAT_RAID._note: Catalogued 2026-08-18 by OTTO from the PHYSICAL box, card by card: 46 individual cards. This replaces the 2026-08-11 reading of Queti's product page, which was wrong in the one way that mattered - see _faces.
COMBAT_RAID._faces: THERE ARE NO TWO-FACED CARDS IN THIS BOX. Every entry is its own physical card, so every quantity here is 1. The product page prints pairs as 'A / B' lines and we read that as one card with two faces; OTTO's box says a Discard card is a SEPARATE card that pairs with its weapon, not the back of it. That mistake also hid four cards entirely - the R6, R7, AC-32 and Type 55 + CC-6 Discards - because a face folded into its parent needs no entry of its own. Do not reintroduce quantityPerBox 0 here on the strength of a listing.
COMBAT_RAID._pilots: FIVE pilots, not three: both Hammerheads and both Onyxes ship. OTTO scanned all five QR codes on 2026-08-18 and they open ids 304 / 364 (Hammerhead), 323 / 365 (Onyx) and 363 (Scout) - exactly the mapping qr_ids.json already held for FPA-04 / FPA-04-2 / LPA-23 / LPA-23-2 / FPA-63. So the '-2' ids remain ours, but they are anchored to the right published card, which is the identity that matters.
COMBAT_RAID._removed: The community data also put ADK15/MAS Porcupine Microwave (161) and ADK30F Tarantula Firepower (163) in this box; neither is in the physical box. Nor is the KK9 Snake Eye Micro Scout (LHDR-KK9), confirmed by OTTO 2026-08-18.
COMBAT_RAID._rl08: The published list writes the chassis as 'RL-08M / RL-08'. The box holds RL-08 and RL-08C as separate cards (534 and 021) and no RL-08M, so the listing's 'M' was a typo and the pairing was two cards all along.
COMBAT_RAID._projectile: 071 MC-3 'Razor' Missile is ONE card (OTTO, 2026-08-18). The product page's '2 Projectiles' counts the MINIATURES - the box holds two models and a single card for them. Card counts and model counts are not the same number, and this is the entry that proves it.

LAB_PD_CRISIS1._note: The retail LAB-CRISIS H2-A box prints 6 Part Cards, 1 Pilot Card, 1 Projectile Card and 4 Projectile miniatures. The community data had only five parts here and filed BOTH HL2 chassis under the H2-B box, which leaves this kit with no legs to stand on. The base HL2 chassis (548) is the sixth card; the two kits share it, which is what the product's modular-magnetic-parts design implies. INFERRED from the printed card count - check a physical box if one turns up. PDAM-002 is the Exocet both backpacks launch. The Pilot Card is Combatant A-70 (XPA-60), confirmed by OTTO 2026-08-10. It was briefly recorded as A-69 on the reading that the H2-A and H2-B contents panels showed the same pilot; they do not, and the panels being near-identical art is exactly why they cannot be told apart at a glance. Read the ID number in the card's corner, not the artwork.

LAB_PD_CRISIS2._note: Restated rather than changed: this file is authoritative per box, so a box named here must list everything it ships. Torso, both chassis, both arms and the backpack are the 6 Part Cards. The Pilot Card is Combatant A-69 (XPA-59), added 2026-08-10: OTTO read the ID number off the box contents panel. H2-A ships A-70, so the two kits take one Combatant each.

_unlisted: MD-4C Reaper Type III (PRDR-102) and MD-4D Reaper Type IV (PRDR-103) were also filed under the Type 1 box, which is wrong, but no box is known to ship them. They are deliberately left with no box rather than guessed into one. Add an entry above if a listing turns up. The PD pilots were the same case until 2026-08-10: the community data filed all three Combatants under H2-B at once, and nothing said which box printed which, so all three were held back. OTTO then read the ID number off each box's contents panel, and our own card scans settled the numbering - XPA-59/60/61 print ID 69/70/71, NOT the A-101/A-102/A-103 the community data gave them. H2-B ships Combatant A-69 and H2-A ships A-70, one each, which is what the boxes' "1 Pilot Card" always implied. A-71 stays unassigned, but ONE OF THE REASONS RECORDED HERE WAS WRONG - corrected the same day. The claim was "the championship 1.02 data publishes only TWO PD torsos, so there is no third PD mech for a third pilot to fly". That was read off the championship XLSX, which is a SUBSET of what exists - it lists championship-legal released parts only. We actually hold SIX PD torsos: H2-A and H2-B, plus the "Chance" wave (PDTR-201 H3-J, PDTR-202 H3-K) and their chassis PDCH-201/202, all flagged UNSALE. So there ARE further PD mechs, a "Chance" kit is a plausible home for A-71, and that line of reasoning is withdrawn. What still holds: the publisher's LAB SERIES page lists ten kits with no "Chance" among them (so the kit is unreleased), the parts lists carry no box or set column at all, only a fluff 'Subordinate' field, which reads 'Operation Squadron 542' for all three Combatants alike; the live API record has NO box or set field in its schema, so that route can never answer this for any card; and neither retailer nor publisher product page itemises card counts. The one source left is physical: whether the H2-B contents panel prints one Pilot Card or two. OTTO has the photos - that single number settles it. Until then a card with no box is treated as "cannot tell, show it" rather than "not owned", which is the right default for a card that is real and championship-legal.
